topicName: Imports vs Includes (Static vs Dynamic Execution)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Ansible Imports vs Includes: Static vs Dynamic Execution"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When writing modular and reusable Ansible playbooks, you often need to split your automation logic into smaller files. Ansible provides two primary mechanisms for this: imports and includes. The fundamental difference lies in when they are processed: imports are static, while includes are dynamic."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Static Execution with Imports"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"An import (such as import_playbook, import_tasks, or import_role) is processed during the parsing phase, before the playbook execution begins. This means Ansible evaluates the imported file's contents into the main playbook tree immediately."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"- name: Execute static task import
  hosts: all
  tasks:
    - name: Import common tasks statically
      import_tasks: common_tasks.yml"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Dynamic Execution with Includes"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"An include (such as include_tasks or include_role) is processed dynamically as the playbook runs, task by task. When Ansible hits an include statement during runtime, it reads and executes the included file at that exact moment."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"- name: Execute dynamic task include
  hosts: all
  tasks:
    - name: Include tasks dynamically based on condition
      include_tasks: conditional_tasks.yml
      when: ansible_os_family == "RedHat""},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Differences and Use Cases"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Loops: Includes work seamlessly with loops because each iteration evaluates dynamically. Imports applied with loops will apply the loop to the import mechanism itself, not individual tasks inside."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Conditionals: When using 'when' statements on an import, the condition is applied to all tasks inside the imported file. On an include, it evaluates whether the include statement itself should run."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Visibility: Static imports show all individual tasks in the --list-tasks output because they are pre-parsed. Dynamic includes only show the include task itself during listing."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use imports (static) by default when you need predictable structure, fast parsing, and visibility into all tasks. Use includes (dynamic) when you require loops, runtime conditional logic, or variable-driven file paths."}]
